trickyParts: The staleness check is deliberately not allowedLogin: that helper answers 400 ASSIGNEE_NOT_ALLOWED, and a default left stale by a restore or a direct write must fall through to nobody rather than refuse the create. After the simplify pass it is a scalar subquery in the returning of the update projects … next_number statement the create already runs, so no statement runs under the project row lock that did not run before, and defaultAssignee is a pure function again.

Both routes are human-only on purpose, for the same reason GET /api/v1/users is: they hand out a person's email address. No agent command, flag or route sets a project's default, and the reason is written at the head of project_default_assignee.go so a later reader does not add one for symmetry with the architecture-source routes.

The browser rows focus the control before selecting an option, as e2e/issue.e2e.ts:973-977 already does for the issue's own assignee picker: the people list is fetched only once a reader reaches for the control, so the option does not exist until then.

Adding a Default assignee column to the Projects table made the existing settings row's getByRole('columnheader', { name: 'Default' }) ambiguous with the repository table's own Default column. That one locator is now exact; nothing else about that row changed.

The picker's write state is per row on purpose: one shared mutation let a failure or pick on one project replace another's error. A row's shown pick overrides the stored value only while that row has a save out or queued; onSettled clears it once nothing is queued, after onSuccess has already written the server's answer into the defaults cache, so the control never flashes the old value. onMutate cancels a defaults read already out, which would otherwise land over the answer.

Unknown means `defaults.data === undefined`, not `!isSuccess`: a refetch that fails after a successful read keeps the last known list on screen beside the load error, which is true, rather than blanking every row.

TanStack v5.102.8: a scoped mutation dispatches status pending with its variables and runs onMutate as soon as mutate is called, and waits in the MutationCache until earlier mutations of its scope finish; hook-level onSuccess/onSettled run before the final status dispatch. So useMutationState's last pending variables is the newest pick from any mount, and the last save's answer is in the cache before it leaves the pending list (no flash).

Superseding is decided inside mutationFn at the save's turn: the newest pending mutation for the key is compared by identity of its variables object (one fresh object per pick). The error survives an unmount because it is read from the MutationCache, which needs gcTime Infinity; onSettled removes every other settled save of the project, so the cache holds at most the newest settled save plus pending ones.
deviations: The plan's D4 said the staleness check would be one exists query run only when the four earlier chain steps had yielded nobody. The ce-simplify-code pass folded it into the returning of the statement the create already runs, so it costs one primary-key probe on people inside a statement that runs regardless, and no second round trip under the project row lock on any create. The behaviour the plan specified is unchanged: a stale default still falls through to nobody, a project with no default still costs nothing, and the chain's order is untouched.

The planner's two recorded departures from the spec stand as written: the prose sweep is fourteen source sites plus the generated claude-envoy bundle rather than the spec's five, and the default is written through a per-project human-only PUT and read through a human-only list route rather than through the architecture-source family's authAny shape.

The architect asked for an explicit-null test beside the absent-body refusal. TestPutProjectDefaultAssigneeSetsChangesAndClears already sends {"assignee": null} and reads the stored default cleared, so no second test of the same path was added; it is the guard against refusing every falsy body.

Round 2's send-every-pick behaviour is reverted as test round 4 and the architect ruled: superseded picks never leave the browser. The implementer's own remount e2e row and two unit tests changed their expected wire order to match; the tester's rows are unmodified.

Where a repository has no mapping that project is DISPATCH_DEFAULT_PROJECT, so a default set there reaches that person for every unmapped repository's issues. The Settings page now says so beside the control, as the architect ruled; whoever sets a default there sees the consequence at the moment they set it.
dispatch issue still cannot say 'nobody' (the tool takes assignee as an optional string with no null). An explicit nobody stays an API capability; no acceptance line asks to change it.
